message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph).
• In cities: 25–35 mph.
• School zones: 20 mph (or 15 mph if a school bus is present). | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Lower BAC limits for commercial drivers (0.04 %) and drivers under 21 (0.02 %). | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.
• At four‑way stops, the first vehicle to arrive has priority. | | **Headlights & Signals** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Turn signals must be used 100 ft before turning. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display valid registration stickers.
• Towing laws require a tow bar or chain and proper lighting. | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of fire hydrants, driveways, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid permit. | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Drivers must remain stopped until the bus moves again. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep to the right lane unless passing.
• Use the left lane for passing only. | | **Traffic Cameras & Speed Cameras** | • Texas uses speed cameras in some counties; fines are issued automatically. | | **Insurance** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage. | | **Special Zones** | • **High‑Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lanes**: 2+ occupants or carpool permits.
• **Construction Zones**: Follow posted signs; speed limits may be reduced. | ### How to Find Specific Laws - **Texas Transportation Code**: The primary source for all traffic statutes. - **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)**: Offers driver’s handbook and updates. - **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)**: Provides licensing rules and vehicle registration info. ### Quick Tips 1. **Always obey posted signs** – they override general rules. 2. **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk on the phone. 3. **Check your state’s handbook** for any recent changes (e.g., new speed limits or DUI penalties). If you need details on a particular law (e.g., “speed limits in Texas school zones” or “DUI penalties for commercial drivers”), let me know and I can dive deeper!
